standard_prerequisites.name: Cosimplicial objects and their cochain complexes
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a cosimplicial object U of an additive category, the associated cochain complex s(U) and, over an abelian category, the complex Q(U).
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the objects of the statement (source lines 5283-5287).

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy and the opposite category
standard_prerequisites.statement: Homotopic morphisms of cosimplicial objects correspond to homotopic morphisms in the opposite category via the contravariant functor A to A (the author's lemma-push-outs-simplicial-object-w-section, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It transports the hypothesis to the opposite category (source lines 5291-5294).

standard_prerequisites.name: The simplicial statement and the identification of the opposites
standard_prerequisites.statement: Homotopic maps of simplicial objects induce homotopic maps on s and on N (the author's lemma-homotopy-s-N, retained as context), together with the identities s(a') = (s(a))' and Q(U)' = N(U').
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the homotopy in the opposite category and the two identifications (source lines 5295-5302).

core_obligations: Transport to the opposite category: use the contravariant functor A to A and the push-out lemma to see that a' and b' are homotopic (source lines 5291-5294).

Apply the simplicial statement: conclude that s(a') and s(b') are homotopic, so s(a) and s(b) are homotopic after identifying s(a') with the opposite of s(a) and applying the double opposite (source lines 5295-5300).
Repeat for Q: obtain the statement for the Q-complexes in the same way from Q(U)' = N(U') (source lines 5300-5302).

proof_roadmap.step: Send the homotopy to the opposite category and quote the push-out lemma.
Use the simplicial statement and the identification s(a') = (s(a))' to conclude for s.
Repeat the argument for the Q-complexes via Q(U)' = N(U').

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-homotopy-s-Q at source lines 5278-5288: for homotopic morphisms a, b : U to V of cosimplicial objects of an additive category, the induced maps on the associated cochain complexes s(U) to s(V) are homotopic, and over an abelian category the same holds for the Q-complexes. The proof at source lines 5290-5303 transfers the statement along the opposite-category functor: in the opposite category the maps a' and b' are homotopic by the push-out lemma, the simplicial version (lemma-homotopy-s-N) then gives homotopic maps s(a') and s(b'), and because s(a') is the opposite of s(a) one concludes by applying the double-opposite functor; the Q-case follows the same way using Q(U)' = N(U'). It is short; the substance is the correct bookkeeping of the opposite functors and the two identifications used to transfer the homotopy back.
